nodes.label: Decision: Self-Hosted WordPress on a Docker VPS
nodes.rationale: Cheapest ongoing cost (~5-12 USD/mo), matches the maintainer's Linux/Docker background, and gives full control over the content-warning gate and image pipeline that managed hosts will not allow customising. A non-technical operator publishes from the WP mobile app while the maintainer owns the server. Do not go below 2 GB RAM; Linode Singapore/Mumbai for latency to Sri Lanka.

nodes.label: Decision: .com Domain (with .lk later)
nodes.rationale: Instant registration, no paperwork, globally trusted by AdSense and search engines; add a .lk and redirect if the operation formalises into a registered business. Bought through Cloudflare Registrar at wholesale (~9-10 USD/yr) or Namecheap.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Proxied DNS (CDN, DDoS, WAF)
nodes.rationale: Proxied (orange cloud) A records are what grant the free CDN, DDoS protection and WAF, and they hide the VPS's real IP - this matters for a site that may host controversial, graphic news content and draw hostile traffic.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Origin Certificate + Full (strict) SSL
nodes.rationale: Encrypts Cloudflare-to-VPS traffic without Let's Encrypt/Certbot renewal automation, since Origin certs last 15 years. Cert and key live at nginx/certs/cloudflare-origin.pem and .key; SSL mode must be Full (strict).

nodes.label: Three-Layer Taxonomy (categories, tags, content flags)
nodes.rationale: Each layer serves a different purpose and must not be mixed: Layer 1 categories are editorial sections powering the header menu, Layer 2 tags are cross-referencing entities powering related articles (2-5 per post, never a one-use tag), Layer 3 content flags are warning metadata not shown in navigation - so a fatal accident post is Category=Crime & Courts plus Flag=Graphic Content, not a choice between them.

nodes.label: content_flag Taxonomy (Graphic Content, Sensitive Topic)
nodes.rationale: Registered by the content-flag-taxonomy mu-plugin as a separate taxonomy with a Content Flags checkbox panel in the post editor sidebar; graphic-content triggers the full-screen gate plus blurred share image, sensitive-topic triggers only a dismissible banner with no blur.

nodes.label: Graphic Content Warning Gate (click-through, session memory)
nodes.rationale: A full-screen click-through gate for graphic-flagged posts. The reader's I-understand decision is stored in sessionStorage, so reloads and back-navigation do not re-prompt, while closing and reopening the browser resets the gate. Gate text follows the site language (Sinhala under a Sinhala WP locale, English otherwise) and strings can be overridden by developers through the ncg_gate_texts filter.

nodes.label: Auto-Blur Social Share Image Fallback
nodes.rationale: When no manually censored social image is uploaded, this fallback generates a heavily blurred plus pixelated copy of the featured image and sets it as og:image. It deliberately overrides Rank Math/Yoast default output (which would use the real featured image) so that even a forgetful operator can never leak the raw graphic image into Facebook link previews.

nodes.label: Censored-Teasers-to-Full-Article Workflow (blurred on Facebook, full on site)
nodes.rationale: Write the post with the real image, set a featured image (required for the auto-blur fallback), tick Graphic Content, then let the manual or automatic blurred social image carry the Facebook link preview. Routine safe posts stay Facebook-only from the mobile app; graphic posts are done on the laptop dashboard because the extra steps are fiddly on a phone.

nodes.label: Google AdSense Monetization via Site Kit
nodes.rationale: AdSense was required once the paywall was ruled out; Site Kit with Auto ads avoids manual ad-zone coding. Graphic-content articles will get restricted ad serving under Google's Shocking Content policy - low or no revenue on those specific posts is expected, not a bug, and revenue is carried by general content.

nodes.label: Legal Pages Required Before AdSense Application
GeneratePress Parent + Gampola Janamadyawediya Child Theme
nodes.rationale: GeneratePress is one of the lightest themes available - every KB saved is bandwidth and load time on a modest self-hosted VPS - and renders Sinhala Unicode correctly out of the box. The child theme cannot activate until the parent is installed, otherwise WordPress silently falls back to a default theme.

nodes.label: Redis Object Cache Plugin
nodes.rationale: Activated from the plugin screen and auto-connects to the redis container through the WP_REDIS_HOST constant already set in docker-compose.yml; cuts database load during traffic spikes.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Plugin Automatic Cache Purge on Publish
nodes.rationale: The official Cloudflare WordPress plugin purges the edge cache when a post is published or updated, so readers see the latest version without manual cache clearing; needs an API token and Automatic Cache Management enabled.

nodes.label: COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME / Volume-Name Coupling with backup.sh
nodes.rationale: COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=gampola-janamadyawediya in .env is what produces the Docker volume name gampola-janamadyawediya_wordpress_data that backup.sh hard-codes; changing it silently breaks backups, so it must be changed in both places or not at all.

nodes.label: Nightly Backup + Off-Site Sync (Backblaze B2)
nodes.rationale: backup.sh dumps the database and archives wp-content nightly via cron, keeping 7 days locally, but a backup living only on the same VPS does not survive that VPS being lost, hacked or destroyed - the commented-out Backblaze B2 sync (a few cents per GB/month) is not optional for a site that is someone's income.

nodes.label: Security Hardening Checklist
nodes.rationale: Firewall limited to 22/80/443 plus fail2ban and unattended-upgrades from deploy.sh, Cloudflare proxy and Full (strict) as edge layers, xmlrpc.php blocked at Nginx, PHP execution blocked under /wp-content/uploads/, security headers set, and all 4 containers healthchecked. Still open: a tested off-site restore and 2FA on the WP admin account.

nodes.label: UptimeRobot HTTPS Monitoring
nodes.rationale: A 5-minute HTTPS monitor gives an email/SMS alert the moment the site is down instead of the operator hearing about it from an angry reader.
